page.layout: One column of verse in italic, centred on the page; a catchword "Per" at the lower right below the last line.

p.i: Pellit humum, laeto sociae clamore sequuntur, Crura coloratis incinctae, & brachia conchis;

Primus it agmen agens lateri cui tinnula pendent Tympana depicto venerabilis ore sacerdos, Ille manu Cemium sublimi in sede videndum Collocat, hinc aras Cerealia liba per artem Sepia rosasque offert, templo quae mystica matres Munera textilibus secum aduexere caniftris.
Tunc genibus super incumbens Regina reflexis Non audituros vocat in vota irrita Diuos Sanctè ferum semel ah sublimi tange flagello Marmoreosque animos, & ahenea pectora rumpe.

At postquam cura insomni, assiduoque labore Instaurata ingens, stetit alto littore classis Lentaque deductae texerunt marmora naues Certus inire viam, ac lustrata relinquere Regna Cristophorus, classem conscendi, & castra moueri Imperat, innumeras frustra Anacaona morandi Inneftit causas, luctusque incendit amaros Nequicquam nullis animum quippe ille moue tur Vocibus, & lacrimas auersa respuit aure.

Tum vero foedata genas, & pectora virgo Scissa manu, fletuque oculos accensa tumentes, Ibis, ait, nec te quicquam Anacaona mouebit? Ibis, & immiti morituraм funere linques Crudelis? quo tendis? & extera littora tentas? Quin etiam dum saeuit hiems turbata procellis

page.notes: The Latin verse has a few doubtful spellings, notably "Sepia" in line 6 of the second stanza (possibly "Sepia" for a printed word read as uncertain) and "morituraм" with a Cyrillic-looking letter, which should read "moriturum". The catchword "Per" is printed at the lower right. Page number and running head are not printed.
